articles.title: ‘I am up for the challenge’: Tushar Deshpande after 5-17, including hat-trick, in Ranji Trophy opener
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Over the years, the Wankhede Stadium has seen plenty of memorable batting and bowling performances in First-Class cricket.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Over the years, the Wankhede Stadium has seen plenty of memorable batting and bowling performances in First-Class cricket. Mumbai pacer Tushar Deshpande's devastating spell against Chandigarh, that saw him take five for 17 in seven fiery overs including a hat-trick, and one wicket in the only over that he bowled in the second innings, on Day two of their Elite Ranji Trophy Group D opening match will rank right amongst the best.Hurting clearly after being overlooked for India A's upcoming tour of New Zealand, Deshpande, bending his back to extract as much life from the juicy, fresh Wankhede track as was possible, fired on all cylinders, ripping out the heart of Chandigarh's batting like knife going through melting butter. Generating healthy pace, the 'Kalyan Express' was all over Chandigarh's batters on Monday.The hat-trick, which included the wickets of Arjun Azad (top-edged a hook to Sylvester D’Souza at long leg), Shivam Bhambri (a superb away going delivery hit the top of off-stump) and Dipender Kush (a fine catch by Yashasvi Jaiswal at first slip) was the icing on the cake for Deshpande, who celebrated his 50th first-class match in grand fashion."It's my 50th first class match today. So it was just in my mind that I wanted to make it special, but it wasn't like a hat-trick and all that, but I was going to give my 100% today. And when I was batting, there were some patches on the wicket where the ball was seeming a bit. So, my only focus was to bowl maximum balls in the right area and it paid dividends today," Deshpande told reporters after the day's play.Deshpande's spirited performance with the ball came after he had a decent outing with the bat on a hot day, after he had stroked a 47-ball 44, which included four fours and two sixes, to reiterate his utility with the bat. Asked if it was a challenging task to give it all with the ball after batting for that long a while earlier, Deshpande bared his ambitions to be considered a genuine allrounder for India in Test cricket."I think it was challenging (to bowl in this heat after batting earlier). It was hot. But if I want to come in the all-rounder category, or I have to show that I can bat, I have to do this thing. So, it's kind of hard work. Or you can say putting in the hard yards with my batting as well. So, yes, I am up for the challenge," he stressed.With national selector SS Das watching Deshpande's exploits from the MCA President's Box, was it a statement performance? "You can call it whatever you want, but the job is half done. We have just put them to follow on, but we have to come again tomorrow, bowl in the right areas and finish the job as early as possible," a focused-looking Deshpande, who took 134 wickets in 49 matches@28.67, with five wicket hauls in first-class match before this match, asserted.Was it disappointing to not be picked for the 'shadow tour' to New Zealand, and did it provide the 'Kalyan Express' with added motivation? "There is always motivation to play Test cricket for India, no matter if I am selected for India A or not. I thought for a day about that, but I have always said that I want to chase performance, not selection. So, I came back to Wankhede again, reset and do my process and bowl again," Deshpande said.Talking about the hat-trick ball, Deshpande, crediting Jaiswal for the fine grab, said, “I want to bowl my best ball, no matter what. I think it was my day. He could have just missed it or would have been beaten by it, but he nicked it to Jaiswal, who took a brilliant catch."Rating his sizzling performance as 'one of the best,' (his best fist class show is six for 70) Deshpande, while elaborating his second hat-trick ball, which was a 'Jaffa,' said, "If you saw, it was a top of the off-stump ball. And for a new batter to get such a ball, it's like a nightmare. As I said, I was just looking to bowl my best balls. And he got out on that."While it's his maiden first-class hat-trick, the 31-year-old Deshpande has achieved the feat earlier in his cricketing career. "I think I've picked (a hat-trick) right from school. I think I've picked a couple of hat-tricks at the club level, one at a summer camp, one in Mushtaq Ali, and one in KSCA Invitational. And now, the first in the Ranji Trophy," he said fondly.While one is used to see him bowl at speeds of around 140 kmph in the IPL, Monday's spell could be the fastest Deshpande has bowled in first-class cricket."I don't know about the speed in the match. But yes, recently when I was playing for India A (against Australia A), I was bowling at about 140s in every style with the red ball. I think it's not always the speed with the red ball. It's about the situation which you come to bowl in. It's not like T20 cricket, that I have to bowl just four overs. I have to bowl throughout the day. So, whatever the situation is, I look at what I can do the best. And accordingly increase or modify my speeds.Having batted well earlier on the same pitch, which had something to offer to the fast bowlers, Deshpande had a fair idea of how to utilise that knowledge in his bowling. "There were some patches in the middle of the grass. The ball was kicking a little bit. And as everyone knows, if you bowl in good areas, fast bowlers and spinners get a little bit of help. So, that help was there, and I thought it would be of maximum use today,” the allrounder explained.Getting off to the perfect start for the season, Deshpande hasn't set any goal for now. "No, I don't keep any number of goals. I just play game by game, do my best every day. And that's how I have been," he said, matter of factly.Sylvester D’Souza finedMeanwhile, pacer Sylvester D’Souza was fined 20% of his match fee for showing dissent against an umpiring decision.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shubman Gill pips Abhishek Sharma to make history with fifth ICC Player of the Month award as Shafali Verma completes India’s double
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Shubman Gill has extended his dominance at the ICC Player of the Month awards, while Shafali Verma has added another individual honour to
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Shubman Gill has extended his dominance at the ICC Player of the Month awards, while Shafali Verma has added another individual honour to India's recent run of success, with the two stars named the men's and women's Players of the Month for September.Gill claimed the award for a record fifth time in the men's category after a sensational ODI series against the West Indies, while Shafali earned her second monthly honour following influential performances in India's Women's Asia Cup and Asian Games triumphs. The double marked the third time India have swept both awards in the same month.Gill's latest recognition puts him alongside West Indies captain Hayley Matthews, who has also won the ICC Player of the Month award five times across the men's and women's categories.Gill's record fifth award after stunning ODI doubleGill's September campaign was headlined by two remarkable innings against the West Indies. He began with a commanding 110 in the opening ODI in Thiruvananthapuram, helping India secure an eight-wicket victory and take a 1-0 lead in the series.The India captain raised the bar in the next match, smashing 223 off just 133 deliveries in a breathtaking display of strokeplay. His innings powered India through a successful chase of 406, with the hosts winning by eight wickets with 39 balls to spare.The double-century was the quickest in ODI history, adding another milestone to Gill's growing list of achievements.“It feels fantastic to win my fifth ICC Player of the Month award, and I am grateful to the panel for this honour. It was immensely satisfying to score those runs and even more special to be part of successful run chases in front of our home fans, whose support always gives us an extra boost,” Gill said.The right-hander also highlighted the evolving demands of ODI cricket and India's preparations for the next men's World Cup.“The pace of ODI cricket has gone up significantly, and you must think on your feet, assess the conditions quickly and adapt to the demands of the pitch and the target. With the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup in southern Africa next year, we are determined to keep raising our standards and build a strong and balanced team capable of rising to the challenges ahead,” he added.Gill's previous monthly awards came in January and September 2023, followed by February and July 2025. His fifth win further extends his record in the men's category.Shafali completes India's double after Asia Cup and Asian Games heroicsShafali's September recognition reflects her impact across two major tournaments, where her aggressive batting and useful contributions with the ball helped India enjoy a successful run.The opener finished as India's leading run-scorer during their Women's Asia Cup-winning campaign, accumulating 360 runs at a strike rate of 184.61. She also picked up six wickets during the period, underlining her all-round contribution.She carried that form into the Asian Games, producing an unbeaten 100 against Bangladesh in the semi-final before scoring 48 in the final against Sri Lanka.“It is an incredible honour to win the ICC Player of the Month award again. It was immensely satisfying to play my part in our victories at the Asia Cup and the Asian Games, and winning this award makes those triumphs even more special,” Shafali said.The award is her second, following her first win in November 2025 after a match-winning performance in the Women's World Cup final against South Africa in Navi Mumbai.“I am excited about the months ahead and determined to keep performing at my best, with the ICC Women’s Champions Trophy in February next year, another tournament to look forward to. The memory of winning the World Cup is still so fresh and special, and I can’t wait to be back on the field for an ICC tournament on home soil. It promises to be an unforgettable experience!” she added.India achieve the award double for third timeIndia's latest sweep is the fifth occasion in the award's history that players from the same cricket board have won both monthly honours, and the third time India have achieved the feat.Jasprit Bumrah and Smriti Mandhana claimed the men's and women's awards in June 2024, while Abhishek Sharma and Mandhana completed the double in September 2025.The September men's shortlist also featured India opener Abhishek Sharma and Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza. Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu and India left-arm spinner Sree Charani were nominated in the women's category.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sri Lanka name new captain for Pakistan Tests! Former skipper Dhananjaya de Silva retained in 15-member squad
articles.summary: Sri Lanka have named a new captain for their upcoming away Test series against Pakistan, with Kusal Mendis set to take charge of the side in the two-match
articles.body: Sri Lanka have named a new captain for their upcoming away Test series against Pakistan, with Kusal Mendis set to take charge of the side in the two-match ICC World Test Championship (WTC) assignment. Former skipper Dhananjaya de Silva, who recently stepped down from the leadership role, has retained his place in the 15-member squad announced on Tuesday.Mendis, 31, already leads Sri Lanka in ODIs and T20Is and will now take over the Test captaincy from the 35-year-old de Silva. The experienced all-rounder decided to relinquish the position a few days ago, saying he wanted to “pass the mantle to the next generation”.The upcoming series will mark Mendis' first assignment as Sri Lanka's Test captain. The visitors will play two Tests in Pakistan from November 9, with Rawalpindi and Lahore hosting the matches as both sides look to improve their positions in the ongoing WTC cycle.Nissanka included subject to fitness; Madushanka returnsBatter Pathum Nissanka has been named in the squad, subject to regaining full fitness before the opening Test. He sustained a hamstring injury during Sri Lanka's ODI series against England last month, leaving his availability for the Pakistan tour uncertain.There is also a recall for left-arm fast bowler Dilshan Madushanka, while Eshan Malinga has earned a place in the touring party. Uncapped wicketkeeper-batter Anjala Bandara has been included, too, after impressive returns in first-class cricket.The 22-year-old has scored 2,239 runs in 46 first-class innings at an average of 65.85, including seven centuries and seven half-centuries. His highest score is an unbeaten 200.However, opener Lahiru Udara, who struck 188 against the West Indies in June, has been left out. Wicketkeeper-batter Niroshan Dickwella has also failed to make the cut.Sri Lanka seek WTC revival against PakistanSri Lanka occupy seventh place in the WTC standings with a points percentage of 33.33, having recorded one win, two defeats and three draws in the current cycle.Pakistan, meanwhile, are at the bottom with a points percentage of 4.63 after two wins and seven defeats. They will look to recover from their recent struggles, including a 0-3 Test series defeat against England in the UK.Sri Lanka will also be keen to bounce back after losing 0-1 to India at home, although they managed to secure a draw in the second Test to avoid a series whitewash.Sri Lanka squad: Kusal Mendis (c), Pathum Nissanka, Pasindu Sooriyabandara, Dinesh Chandimal, Kamindu Mendis, Sonal Dinusha, Dhananjaya De Silva, Anjala Bandara, Keshara Nuwantha, Prabath Jayasuriya, Milan Rathnayaka, Lahiru Kumara, Asitha Fernando, Dilshan Madushanka, Eshan Malinga.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Indian women’s captain Smriti Mandhana gets new role at UNICEF, says 'every child deserves to dream big'
articles.summary: UNICEF India on Sunday named Indian women’s cricket captain Smriti Mandhana as its Celebrity Advocate on the occasion of the International Day of the Girl.
articles.body: UNICEF India on Sunday named Indian women’s cricket captain Smriti Mandhana as its Celebrity Advocate on the occasion of the International Day of the Girl.Through this role, she will promote equal opportunities for girls and support efforts to improve their health, well-being, education and leadership."I am deeply honoured to join UNICEF India as a Celebrity Advocate. Growing up playing cricket taught me that every dream begins with an opportunity. With hard work, determination, and encouragement, that opportunity can turn into something extraordinary. Every child and young person deserves the chance to dream big and reach their full potential," Mandhana said.Focus on girls’ rights and opportunitiesMandhana has previously supported UNICEF-ICC campaigns promoting gender equality and life skills, along with UNICEF’s Promise to Children campaign. As a Celebrity Advocate, she will continue working to ensure girls have the freedom and support to learn, play and achieve their ambitions."Smriti’s journey from an aspiring young athlete to a global cricket icon demonstrates to girls what is possible when talent meets opportunity. At a time when India is home to the world’s largest generation of children and young people, investing in girls’ rights, leadership, and wellbeing is a nation’s smartest investment. We look forward to partnering with Smriti to help ensure every girl has the opportunity to learn, play, lead, and fulfill her potential," said UNICEF India Representative Cynthia McCaffrey.Mandhana’s achievements in cricketMandhana, an Arjuna Award recipient, was appointed captain of the Indian women’s cricket team earlier this week after Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down. She was also part of the team that won India’s first-ever ICC Women’s Cricket World Cup title in 2025.In the same year, Mandhana became the first woman to score more than 1,000 ODI runs in a calendar year, setting a record with five centuries. In 2026, she emerged as the leading run-scorer in women’s international cricket and women’s T20 internationals.She is also the world’s top-ranked women’s ODI batter and a two-time ICC Women’s Cricketer of the Year.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Spencer Johnson hopes IPL experience will make him better
articles.summary: PUDUCHERRY: As Mitchell Starc comes to the back-end of his career, Australia left-arm pacer Spencer Johnson is building himself up to take over the mantle
articles.body: PUDUCHERRY: As Mitchell Starc comes to the back-end of his career, Australia left-arm pacer Spencer Johnson is building himself up to take over the mantle from the southpaw. Johnson, though, is himself 30 and his journey has been repeatedly interrupted by injuries.His latest assignment with Australia ‘A’ in Puducherry offered a glimpse of what he can bring to the table. On a surface that offered little encouragement to fast bowlers, Johnson extracted disconcerting bounce and troubled India A’s batters, finishing with five wickets across his two appearances. His match-winning spell of 3-35 in the second unofficial ODI earned him the Player of the Match award and helped Australia ‘A’ clinch the series.Having represented Chennai Super Kings in the IPL 2026, Johnson was familiar with the conditions. The paceman was drafted in by CSK last season when Nathan Ellis got injured. The bowler remains grateful for an unforgettable interaction with MS Dhoni, who once invited younger players to his room to discuss his career and approach to the game. “He was very relaxed and approachable. He made me feel like home. It is a memory I will cherish for the rest of my life,” Spencer told TOI.In 2024, he was bought by Gujarat Titans for Rs 10 crores, but he finished with only four wickets in five games.“Regardless of the price tag, there is always pressure because a team has put its faith in you. You want to perform and repay that trust. The IPL is the best tournament in the world, and the more exposure I get to playing in India against the best batters and bowlers, the better I hope my performances will become,” he said.The transition from Australia’s chilly winter to India’s oppressive heat presented another test. “We were training in temperatures of four or five degrees, almost bowling in jumpers. Coming here has been a completely different experience. These are probably the toughest conditions (Puducherry) we have encountered, so getting through them should hold us in good stead for the rest of the season,” he said.Consistency, however, remains his biggest challenge. His international opportunities have been sporadic, with a back stress fracture forcing him to spend 12 months on the sidelines.“The medical staff in Australia always have a plan in place. When I return, the focus is on making sure I am physically stronger than before. There is always a silver lining, and I want to play as much cricket as possible without interruptions,” Spencer said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ranji Trophy 2026-27: Mumbai vice-captain Ayush Mhatre ruled out for a month with hamstring injury
articles.summary: MUMBAI: In a major setback for Mumbai at the start of the Ranji Trophy season, their newly appointed vice-captain Ayush Mhatre has suffered a recurrence
articles.body: MUMBAI: In a major setback for Mumbai at the start of the Ranji Trophy season, their newly appointed vice-captain Ayush Mhatre has suffered a recurrence of his right hamstring injury and has been ruled out for a month. The setback means the young opener is set to miss Mumbai’s remaining three matches of the first leg of the Ranji Trophy, TOI has learnt.The recurrence is a big blow for Mhatre, who was recently named Siddhesh Lad’s deputy for the Ranji Trophy by the Mumbai selectors.The top-order batter had earlier suffered a hamstring injury while playing for Chennai Super Kings (CSK), which ruled him out of the second half of IPL 2026. He was subsequently out of action for almost five months, missing the T20 Mumbai tournament in June, India A’s tour of Sri Lanka and the Duleep Trophy in August.Mhatre sustained the injury after scoring 48 on the opening day of Mumbai’s first-innings effort against Chandigarh at the Wankhede Stadium. He did not take the field on the second and third days of the Ranji Trophy 2026-27 match. The 19-year-old underwent scans on Monday, while substitute Suved Parkar fielded in his place.At the time of his injury during IPL 2026, Mhatre was CSK’s leading run-scorer in the tournament, with 201 runs in six innings at a strike rate of 177.87.Mhatre had undergone rehabilitation at the Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru. The Mumbai Cricket Association’s (MCA) physio cleared him to return to the Ranji Trophy after he featured in the final round of the Kanga League, scoring 25 for Sainath Cricket Club in a ‘B’ Division match.His latest injury could open the door for in-form Kolkata Knight Riders opener Angkrish Raghuvanshi, 22, to earn a call-up for Mumbai’s next Ranji Trophy match against Himachal Pradesh in Bilaspur from October 18 to 21. Raghuvanshi has struck back-to-back double centuries, scoring 203 and 201 for the Rest of India Under-23 team against Tamil Nadu in Chennai and for the Mumbai Under-23 side against Bengal in Kolkata on Tuesday, respectively.At Mumbai’s pre-season press conference, Mhatre had spoken about his preparations following a lengthy injury layoff. With captain Siddhesh Lad seated beside him, he said, "I was in the nets for three weeks. So, the preparation is going really well. And I have got some games also in the CoE. We (the Mumbai team) played at MCA-BKC also. So, it was really good for us to spend some time on the ground. So, we are well prepared."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Smriti Mandhana retains no. 1 spot in ICC ODI rankings; Ellyse Perry returns to top 10
articles.summary: Newly appointed India women’s captain Smriti Mandhana continued to lead the ICC women’s ODI batting rankings, holding on to the top position with 790
articles.body: Newly appointed India women’s captain Smriti Mandhana continued to lead the ICC women’s ODI batting rankings, holding on to the top position with 790 rating points in the latest update released on Tuesday. Australia’s Ellyse Perry also made a return to the top 10, highlighting the latest changes in the rankings.Mandhana, who recently succeeded Harmanpreet Kaur as India’s captain, remains the country’s highest-ranked batter in the 50-over format. Harmanpreet is the only other Indian in the ODI batting top 10, occupying ninth place with 652 points.In the women’s ODI bowling rankings, India all-rounder Deepti Sharma dropped one place to ninth. Australia’s Annabel Sutherland and Megan Schutt, meanwhile, climbed the rankings to strengthen their positions among the leading bowlers.Three Indian batters feature in T20I top 10India also had a strong presence in the women’s T20I batting rankings, with three players securing places in the top 10. Shafali Verma led the Indian contingent in fourth position with 759 points, followed by Mandhana in fifth with 754. Harmanpreet completed the list of Indian batters at 10th, with 656 points.The T20I bowling rankings continued to be dominated by Indian spinners, with Shree Charani occupying the top spot with 817 rating points. Deepti followed her in second place with 754 points, giving India the leading two positions in the category.Deepti was also the only Indian to feature in the top 10 of the women’s T20I all-rounders’ rankings, where she is placed fourth. She ranked sixth in the corresponding ODI all-rounders’ list.India remained third in both the women’s ODI and T20I team rankings.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Australia vs England: Jacob Bethell returns as Thomas Rew and Eddie Jack get call-ups
articles.summary: Jacob Bethell will return for England's white-ball tour of Australia, while there are also first international call-ups for exciting prospects Thomas Rew and Eddie Jack.
articles.body:
Jacob Bethell will return for England's white-ball tour of Australia, while there are also first international call-ups for exciting prospects Thomas Rew and Eddie Jack.

Warwickshire's Bethell has not played since suffering a knee injury in July but is back as part of a near-full-strength squad for three one-day internationals.

England have made changes for the five T20s, resting players ahead of the Test tour of South Africa, meaning 18-year-old Somerset wicketkeeper-batter Rew and Hampshire's 21-year-old pace bowler Jack are included.

"Thomas Rew is an amazing young talent," national selector Marcus North told the Test Match Special podcast. "He has a great maturity around him for an 18-year-old.

"Eddie Jack is another great example of a system that has been supporting and developing our fast bowlers. This is an exciting time – it's always great when you get an opportunity to bring some players in."

The tour begins with the first ODI in Perth on 13 November and ends with the final T20 in Canberra on 2 December – a week before England's warm-up match in South Africa leading into a three-Test series.

There will be live ball-by-ball commentary from every match of England's tour of Australia on Test Match Special.

England white-ball coach Brendon McCullum had previously confirmed he wanted a strong team for the ODI leg of the trip to Australia in the build-up to the World Cup in southern Africa next year.

The New Zealander also conceded he would have to rotate his squad for the T20 leg, given England's schedule in a busy winter of five separate overseas tours.

One-day squad: Harry Brook (Yorkshire – captain), Jofra Archer (Sussex), Gus Atkinson (Surrey), Sonny Baker (Hampshire), Tom Banton (Somerset), Jacob Bethell (Warwickshire), Jordan Cox (Essex), Henry Crocombe (Surrey), Sam Curran (Surrey), Liam Dawson (Hampshire), Ben Duckett (Nottinghamshire), Will Jacks (Surrey), Jamie Overton (Surrey), Adil Rashid (Yorkshire), Joe Root (Yorkshire), Josh Tongue (Nottinghamshire).

T20 squad: Harry Brook (Yorkshire – captain), Tom Banton (Somerset), Jacob Bethell (Warwickshire), James Coles (Sussex), Jordan Cox (Essex), Henry Crocombe (Surrey), Sam Curran (Surrey), Liam Dawson (Hampshire), Aneurin Donald (Derbyshire), Eddie Jack (Hampshire), Will Jacks (Surrey), Jamie Overton (Surrey), Adil Rashid (Yorkshire), Thomas Rew (Somerset), Phil Salt (Lancashire), Luke Wood (Lancashire).

Rusty or something more? South Africa's concern after Australia loss

Exciting Rew in line for history-making debut

For the ODIs, Jofra Archer is back in the pace attack after being rested for the tri-series in Pakistan in October.

Archer's return means the 50-over squad is close to full strength, bar the absence of wicketkeeper Jos Buttler who is set for a lengthy spell on the sidelines following hamstring surgery.

After the ODIs, all of seamers Archer, Gus Atkinson, Josh Tongue and Sonny Baker, along with batter Ben Duckett, miss out on the T20s in order to prepare for South Africa.

The re-shuffle means eye-catching call-ups for Rew and Jack, while opener Aneurin Donald keeps his place after making his debut in the series against Sri Lanka last month.

The addition of Rew and Jack, who were awarded development central contracts on Monday, offers the tantalising prospect of a first international cap against England's fiercest rivals in one of the most iconic venues in cricket. The first T20 is at the colossal Melbourne Cricket Ground on 21 November.

Rew does not turn 19 until 29 November. If he plays on the tour, he would become the third-youngest man to make his England debut in any format after Rehan Ahmed and Brian Close, and the youngest man to play for England against Australia.

Rew is the younger brother of James, who made his Test debut for England against New Zealand at The Oval in June.

Thomas captained England Under-19s to the final of the World Cup earlier this year and made two centuries for Somerset in the County Championship during the summer.

Jack, who has the middle name Vaughan after former England captain Michael, has been on England's radar since last year.

He looks likely to earn a debut in Australia because he is one of only three specialist fast bowlers in the squad. Uncapped Henry Crocombe is down under for both series after earning a two-year central contract on Monday, while Luke Wood is part of the T20 squad despite losing his central deal.

Bethell's return to both squads is an indication of the selection decision England will face for the Test series in South Africa.

In the left-hander's absence for the home Test series against Pakistan this summer, Emilio Gay, Jordan Cox and Dan Lawrence came into the England XI. Bethell's comeback could displace any one of that trio.

"It's a fantastic position to be in," added North. "We haven't sat down and discussed the nuances and detail around that.

"It's a nice problem to have in that we want to have that depth and challenging conversations around selection. It reflects we're in a good place. Around that first Test in South Africa there will be lots of discussions and debates and we'll see where that final XI lands."

Harry Brook captains England on both legs of the tour and is once again set to play across formats in every game of the winter. He has not missed an international since a raft of players were rested for the T20 series in Ireland last September.

The trip will be Brook's first return to Australia since a nightclub incident in Wellington, New Zealand, last October was revealed on the final day of the Ashes series in January.

During the Ashes, England's players came under intense scrutiny from the local media, not helped by a series of off-field misdemeanours. Though a white-ball tour will not have the same profile as the Ashes, the tourists can still expect a degree of hostility from the home fans.

There will also be the spectre of former Test captain Ben Stokes, whose stint with Adelaide Strikers in the Big Bash League begins shortly after England's tour ends.

articles.title: SA vs AUS: Steve Smith cleared of concussion after helmet blow, returns to field in Durban Test
articles.summary: Former Australia captain Steve Smith has been cleared of concussion and resumed fielding duties on the fifth day of the first Test against South Africa at
articles.body: Former Australia captain Steve Smith has been cleared of concussion and resumed fielding duties on the fifth day of the first Test against South Africa at Kingsmead in Durban on Tuesday, after undergoing a series of clinical assessments following a blow to the helmet.The 37-year-old batter was struck by a short-pitched delivery from Anrich Nortje during Australia's second innings. Smith attempted to duck under the ball but misjudged its trajectory as it failed to rise as much as he expected.Although he continued batting after the incident, scoring 27 off 41 balls before being caught at long-on off Simon Harmer, Smith did not take the field when South Africa began their second innings on Monday. Michael Neser served as his substitute fielder during that session.However, Smith returned to the field on Tuesday morning after being cleared under Cricket Australia's concussion protocols. He was stationed in the slip cordon when South Africa resumed their chase and subsequently took a catch to dismiss Kyle Verreynne off Matt Renshaw's bowling."Steve Smith has undergone a series of clinical assessments over the past 24 hours in accordance with Cricket Australia’s concussion protocols and has been cleared to take the field this morning," Cricket Australia said in a statement.Smith's concussion history raises concern after helmet blowThe incident brought back memories of Smith's previous concussion scare during the 2019 Ashes in England, when he was struck on the head by fast bowler Jofra Archer and forced to miss part of a Test match.Smith's return to the field came after medical assessments over the preceding 24 hours, with Australia following the prescribed protocols before allowing the experienced batter to resume his duties.His presence was a boost for Australia as they pushed for victory in the series opener, with South Africa mounting a determined resistance on the final day.Australia close in on victory as South Africa lose two wicketsSouth Africa resumed at 102/4 on Tuesday, needing another 319 runs to win. They reached 166/6 by lunch after Australia struck twice to strengthen their grip on the contest.Opener Aiden Markram led the home side's resistance, remaining unbeaten on 69 at the interval alongside Marco Jansen on seven. The pair had to rebuild after Wiaan Mulder's patient 69-run fifth-wicket partnership with Markram ended when Josh Hazlewood had Mulder caught behind by Alex Carey.Part-time spinner Matt Renshaw then dismissed Verreynne, who made just one before edging a reckless shot to Smith at slip.Renshaw has been Australia's standout performer with the bat, having scored 190 in the first innings and 82 in the second, before adding two wickets to his match contribution.Australia needed four more wickets at lunch to seal victory in the opening Test. The second Test of the series is scheduled to begin in Gqeberha on Sunday.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England name squads for Australia tour: Jofra Archer, Jacob Bethell return; Thomas Rew earns maiden call-up
articles.summary: England have recalled Jofra Archer and Jacob Bethell to their ODI squad for the November tour of Australia as they step up preparations for next year’s
articles.body: England have recalled Jofra Archer and Jacob Bethell to their ODI squad for the November tour of Australia as they step up preparations for next year’s ODI World Cup. While Archer has been rested for the upcoming tri-series in Pakistan, Bethell returns after recovering from the knee injury he sustained during the ODI series against India in July.Harry Brook will lead a 16-member ODI squad that is expected to be close to full strength. However, England will be without Jos Buttler, who is recovering from recent hamstring surgery, and Saqib Mahmood, who has been sidelined by a knee injury.England have also announced their T20I squad for the tour, with four uncapped players earning selection.Archer, Bethell return as England strengthen ODI squadArcher’s return bolsters England’s pace attack ahead of their preparations for the 2027 ODI World Cup, while Bethell’s inclusion adds another option to the batting line-up following his recovery from injury.England national selector Marcus North said the return of the duo would allow the side to approach the ODI series at close to full strength as they build towards next year’s global tournament.“The returns of Jacob Bethell and Jofra Archer for the ODI series means that we will be at close to full strength as we ramp up preparations for a World Cup in a year’s time,” North said.However, Archer, Gus Atkinson, Sonny Baker and Josh Tongue will not feature in the subsequent T20I series as England manage their fast bowlers ahead of the Test tour of South Africa.England ODI squad: Harry Brook (c), Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson, Sonny Baker, Tom Banton, Jacob Bethell, Jordan Cox, Henry Crocombe, Sam Curran, Liam Dawson, Ben Duckett, Will Jacks, Jamie Overton, Adil Rashid, Joe Root, Josh Tongue.Four uncapped players named in England T20I squadEngland have introduced fresh faces to their T20I set-up, with Rew and Jack earning their maiden international call-ups. Rew, 18, is the youngest member of the squad and received his first ECB central contract a day before the announcement.Rew captained England to the final of the ICC Men's Under-19 World Cup in February. Both he and Jack were also part of the England Lions squad that toured Australia last year.Salt returns after recovering from the quad injury that ruled him out of England’s 3-0 T20I series win over Sri Lanka last month. Aneurin Donald has retained his place after making his international debut during that series, while Wood has also been recalled. North said England were keen to test themselves against Australia in their home conditions, pointing to the team’s recent form under Brook’s leadership.“Our T20 team has been in excellent form under captain Harry Brook and we are looking forward to the opportunity to test ourselves in Australian conditions against a very good team,” he said.England T20I squad: Harry Brook (c), Tom Banton, Jacob Bethell, James Coles, Jordan Cox, Henry Crocombe, Sam Curran, Liam Dawson, Aneurin Donald, Eddie Jack, Will Jacks, Jamie Overton, Adil Rashid, Thomas Rew, Phil Salt, Luke Wood.England's Australia tour scheduleEngland’s white-ball tour will begin with a warm-up match at the WACA in Perth on November 7. The three-match ODI series will be played in Perth, Adelaide and Hobart before the teams switch to the shortest format.The five-match T20I series will begin at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on November 21, with subsequent matches scheduled in Gold Coast, Brisbane, Sydney and Canberra.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'He never chased that reward': Ashwin reveals what drove Bhuvneshwar Kumar's India comeback
articles.summary: Ravichandran Ashwin believes Bhuvneshwar Kumar's return to India's T20I setup is a reward for his consistency rather than the result of chasing an
articles.body: Ravichandran Ashwin believes Bhuvneshwar Kumar's return to India's T20I setup is a reward for his consistency rather than the result of chasing an international comeback. The veteran pacer earned a recall to the national squad after impressing for Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) in the IPL, with Ashwin crediting his focus on performance for his return.Bhuvneshwar's selection for India's upcoming five-match T20I series against New Zealand, beginning next week, was one of the major talking points following the squad announcement. The right-arm pacer is set to return to international T20 cricket after a gap of four years.'He has gone on his own journey'Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ashwin suggested that Bhuvneshwar remained focused on improving his bowling and fulfilling his responsibilities for RCB rather than worrying about a potential India recall."I have a feeling that Bhuvneshwar Kumar hasn't even thought about a comeback. I think this will be his mantra for success. And when I'm watching him from afar, I have also experienced this myself, he has gone on his own journey," Ashwin said."He has focused on doing well, bowling well with the new ball and performing for RCB. Whatever he could do, he did it. His recall is the reward for his success. He never chased that reward; he simply did his job and success followed," he added.Ashwin backs India for 2027 ODI World Cup, picks South Africa as serious contendersLooking ahead to the 2027 ODI World Cup, Ashwin backed India to challenge for the title but warned that hosts South Africa could pose a significant threat in familiar conditions.Ashwin pointed to India's pace-bowling resources, spin options and batting experience as reasons to believe the team can mount a strong campaign. He particularly highlighted Bumrah's importance, suggesting that the fast bowler could make a major difference if he performs at his best."India has the ability. If Jasprit Bumrah is firing on all cylinders, he will have a good fast-bowling experience. India has a good spin stock. There, in a lot of grounds, you will get the help of spin. There is experience in batting," he said.However, Ashwin identified South Africa as one of the strongest contenders, citing home advantage, familiarity with local conditions and the experience players have gained through the SA20 league."I will honestly say that two-three teams look good to me. Out of them, South Africa is the best. I think South Africa will be a serious contender for the home World Cup. So India will have to play against the South African team," he said."South Africa, in South African conditions, especially after SA20, have the skills, they know all the conditions, they play good cricket and the team looks together. That's a very strong force in cricket," Ashwin added.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: South Africa vs Australia: Josh Hazlewood claims career-best Test figures of 6-49 as Australia take 1-0 series lead
articles.summary: Australia beat South Africa by 214 runs in first Test of three-match series as Josh Hazlewood's career-best 6-49 seals victory on final day in Durban; Watch day one of the second Test from Gqeberha, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 8am, Sunday, with play starting at 9am
articles.body:
Australia went into the final day in Durban requiring six more wickets for victory, and South Africa a hugely unlikely 319 further runs to win, and though the visitors encountered some resistance from Aiden Markram (75) in particular, they eventually wrapped things up shortly after lunch.

Josh Hazlewood (6-49) took four of the wickets to fall to finish with career-best figures, including the opening breakthrough of Wiaan Mulder (29) - caught down the legside - to end his and Markram's 69-run stand that offered South Africa some brief hope of clinging on for a draw.

Kyle Verreynne would depart just three balls later, out to Player of the Match and part-time spinner Matt Renshaw (2-30), but the collapse was delayed until the other side of lunch as Markram found further support in Marco Jansen (35).

The pair put on 45 for the seventh wicket until Hazlewood's return, with the second new ball in hand, signalled the end of South Africa's resistance as he removed Jansen and Simon Harmer, for a duck, in the same over.

Jansen was bowled through the gate by a devastating nip-backer, a delivery that was bettered only by the vicious bouncer that did for Harmer third ball - gloved to Alex Carey.

Markram's 237-ball stay at the crease would then be ended by Mitchell Starc (1-33) - out on review, inside-edging behind - as South Africa lost their final four wickets for five runs in litte more than two overs, Hazlewood fittingly wrapping things up with the dismissal of Anrich Nortje.

Renshaw claimed Player of the Match honours due to his magnificent 190 that rescued Australia from 124-6 on day one, as they were eventually bowled out for 390 and secured a 106-run first innings lead. He'd add 82 in the second innings.

South Africa will hope to have pace attack spearhead Kagiso Rabada back for the second Test in Gqeberha, which starts on Sunday live on Sky Sports, after he missed the series opener due to his ongoing recovery from a hamstring injury suffered in June.

Cummins: Win was built on Renshaw hundred

"It was a great win. A lot of it was built on what Matt Renshaw did on day one, and we managed to hold onto that lead for the rest of it.

"Everywhere I look [with the bowling attack], there's a lot of Test wickets there - even our part-timers are better than that. I've got loads of options and Hazlewood is just a captain's dream.

"Two games left, anything can still happen, but being ahead in the series always makes things a little easier."

Bavuma: Don't let Australia lead from the front

"It's not the way we wanted to start. You've got to give it to the Australians and the way they dominated the majority of the game.

"The way they got stuck into us, even after they were 124-6 [in the first innings], they showed their experience, showed their skills and got themselves into a very competitive position.

"For a lot of us who have the experience of playing against them, you don't want to give them that opportunity to lead from the front.

"There's a lot of questions and conversations we'll need to have - we can learn from them on a batting and bowling point view - but you've got to give it to them in terms of their performance."

articles.title: Josh Hazlewood wreaks havoc on Day 5 as Australia crush South Africa by 214 runs in Durban
articles.summary: Josh Hazlewood produced a match-winning spell on Day 5 to guide Australia to a 214-run victory over South Africa in the Durban Test on Tuesday.
articles.body: Josh Hazlewood produced a match-winning spell on Day 5 to guide Australia to a 214-run victory over South Africa in the Durban Test on Tuesday. The Australian pacer claimed six wickets for 49 runs, registering his best bowling figures in Test cricket and handing South Africa captain Temba Bavuma his first defeat in the format as skipper.Chasing a target of 421, South Africa were bowled out for 206 in the second session, despite a fighting 75 from Aiden Markram. Hazlewood dismantled the lower order to seal Australia's dominant victory after the hosts had shown some resistance during the final day's play.Hazlewood dismantles South Africa's lower orderSouth Africa resumed Day 5 hoping to extend their resistance, with Markram and Wiaan Mulder attempting to keep Australia at bay. However, Hazlewood removed Mulder for 29, ending a 204-ball partnership and opening the door for the visitors.Steve Smith then took another outstanding catch in the slips to dismiss Kyle Verreynne, leaving South Africa struggling at 156/6. Marco Jansen briefly delayed Australia's victory, batting alongside Markram to take the contest beyond the morning session. Hazlewood, however, broke through again, bowling Jansen with a delivery that seamed back sharply before dismissing Simon Harmer in the same over.Mitchell Starc subsequently ended Markram's resistance, with the opener departing after facing 237 deliveries. Hazlewood completed the victory by dismissing Anrich Nortje, finishing with career-best figures of 6/49 and his 15th five-wicket haul in Tests.Renshaw sets up Australia's victoryAustralia's win was built on Matt Renshaw's outstanding batting performance. He scored 190 in the first innings as Australia posted 390, before adding another 82 in the second innings to help the visitors declare at 314/6. South Africa had managed 284 in their first innings but struggled to sustain their chase of 421. David Bedingham contributed 46, while Markram provided the bulk of the resistance with his determined knock.For South Africa, Wiaan Mulder claimed 4/68 in Australia's first innings, while Anrich Nortje and Keshav Maharaj took two wickets each in the second. Australia's commanding performance with both bat and ball secured a comprehensive victory, with Renshaw's runs and Hazlewood's decisive final-day spell proving instrumental.Brief scores: Australia 390 and 314/6 declared beat South Africa 284 and 206 by 214 runs. Matt Renshaw scored 190 and 82, while Josh Hazlewood returned figures of 6/49 in the second innings.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: South Africa vs Australia: The questions posed after Proteas' heavy defeat
articles.summary: Australia complete 214-run victory over South Africa in Durban. What does heavy defeat mean for the world champions?
articles.body:
Australia 390 & 314-6 dec: Renshaw 82; Nortje 2-56, Maharaj 2-56

South Africa 284 & 206: Markram 75; Hazlewood 6-49

South Africa's 12-match unbeaten run came to a shuddering stop with defeat against Australia in Durban, but were they simply rusty or is there more to read into a Test match in which they were outclassed across the five days?

The world champions held on until an hour into the afternoon session on the final day – Aiden Markram fought admirably for 237 deliveries – but Australia, led by Josh Hazlewood with career-best figures of 6-49, eventually broke any lingering resistance to go 1-0 up in the three-match series.

"I would like to see more fight," said Proteas coach Shukri Conrad. "I don't know if it is alarming [but] it is concerning."

So should South Africa be worried at the start of an eye-catching few months which includes the visit of England over Christmas?

Much was made of South Africa's run to the 2025 World Test Championship final at Lord's.

They played only 12 Tests – no team played fewer – and qualified after drawing at home against India and losing in New Zealand, before beating West Indies, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Pakistan.

Mitigation for this latest Test also comes from the fact this is their first in almost a year and the majority of their batters played one domestic red-ball match to prepare.

Australia recently came off an eight-month break of their own and lost to Bangladesh in home conditions, as Conrad was keen to point out.

And last summer's famous win over Australia and a 2-0 success in India proves they can beat the world's top teams.

However, this Test only reinforced a worrying trend among South Africa's batters.

Tristan Stubbs and Ryan Rickelton are fine white-ball players, but Stubbs' two Test centuries have come against Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, and Rickelton's against Sri Lanka and Pakistan.

In the first innings, Stubbs, two overs after Wiaan Mulder had been bounced out, top-edged a pull to fine leg, and in the second he played a loose drive on one.

Opener Rickelton drove and edged at a wide ball late on day two and nicked through a pull in the fourth over on day four.

Similarly, Mulder scored 367 not out against Zimbabwe last year, but Bangladesh are the only other side he averages more than 30 against. His 110-ball stay for 29 on the final day before being strangled down the leg side was at least encouraging.

Wicketkeeper Kyle Verreynne, in contrast, lasted only three balls before nudging Matt Renshaw's part-time spin to slip. His Test average of 30.14 drops to 28 against Australia and 15 against both England and India.

Conrad said that "a few of the guys need to step up".

"The real disappointment was the batting in the first dig on a really good wicket," Conrad said.

"Yes, a world-class attack, but quite a few guys getting starts and not kicking on."

Aiden Markram's defiant knock in the fourth innings, in which he batted for almost six hours for 75 runs before edging Mitchell Starc through to Alex Carey in the afternoon session, was one positive for the Proteas.

David Bedingham also looked comfortable in his new position of number three, albeit he was one of those guilty of failing to make the most of starts after reaching 49 and 46.

This defeat was not solely on the batters, either.

Bavuma, who tasted defeat as captain for the first time in this match, allowed the game to drift on day two as Australia extended their score from 124-6 to 390 not out.

Australia's Matt Renshaw played brilliantly for his 190 but was not challenged as he casually farmed the strike and protected Nathan Lyon in their ninth-wicket stand of 134.

And while judging them against Australia's fearsome attack, the most successful quartet Test cricket has seen, is hardly fair, South Africa's bowlers lacked the relentless pressure of their counterparts.

Anrich Nortje was impressive in taking four wickets in his first Test since March 2023. His last spell was quicker than his first as he brought pace and hostility, hitting Steve Smith on the helmet with a bouncer on day four.

But Mulder offered little after his new-ball spells and Marco Jansen was quiet after dismissing Nic Maddinson and Steve Smith on day one.

The return from injury of their premier quick Kagiso Rabada, who was seen bowling at lunch on day five, cannot come soon enough.

Spinners Simon Harmer and Keshav Maharaj did not escape Conrad's gaze either.

"Anrich's return was phenomenal and really pleasing," Conrad said.

"If we were brutally honest, our spinners were not as sharp as they normally are."

With the second Test starting in only five days' time in Gqeberha, South Africa must hope this Test has removed the rust.

The alternate takeaway would be far more concerning.

articles.title: Yuvraj Singh joins Delhi Capitals coaching staff ahead of new IPL season, reunites with franchise after 11 years
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh has joined Delhi Capitals as their Assistant and Batting Coach ahead of the upcoming Indian Premier
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh has joined Delhi Capitals as their Assistant and Batting Coach ahead of the upcoming Indian Premier League season, marking his first formal coaching role in his career.The appointment was officially announced by the JSW and GMR co-owned franchise on Tuesday. The Times of India had reported the development earlier in June, with the franchise now confirming Yuvraj's appointment.A veteran of 304 ODIs, 40 Tests and 58 T20Is, Yuvraj was a key architect of India's triumphs at the 2007 ICC T20 World Cup and the 2011 ICC Cricket World Cup. The 44-year-old has also mentored several established and emerging Indian cricketers in recent years, and will now make his IPL coaching debut with Delhi Capitals.The appointment also marks a reunion with the franchise for Yuvraj. In 2015, Delhi Daredevils, as the team was then known, signed him for a record Rs 16 crore, making him the most expensive player in IPL history at the time. He went on to represent the franchise in all 14 matches that season.Parth Jindal welcomes Yuvraj to Delhi CapitalsSpeaking on the appointment, Delhi Capitals chairman and co-owner, and JSW Sports founder, Parth Jindal, expressed his delight at bringing the former India all-rounder into the coaching setup."We are absolutely thrilled to welcome Yuvi to the Delhi Capitals family. Yuvi is one of Indian cricket’s greatest match-winners and someone who has played a pivotal role in mentoring many of the brightest young talents in Indian cricket today. His experience, winning mindset, and ability to connect with players will be invaluable to our squad."We wish him all the very best as he takes on his first formal coaching role, and we are excited to begin this new chapter together. His return to the franchise also marks a special moment for everyone associated with the Capitals, and we look forward to seeing him work with Dada and the rest of the staff going forward," Jindal said.Kiran Kumar Grandhi, co-owner of Delhi Capitals and founder of GMR Sports, also welcomed Yuvraj, highlighting his experience and competitive spirit."We are delighted to welcome Yuvraj Singh to Delhi Capitals as our Assistant & Batting Coach. His remarkable career, competitive spirit and deep understanding of the game make him a tremendous addition to our coaching setup."This marks his first formal coaching role in the IPL, and we are confident that his insights, winning mindset and ability to mentor players will make a meaningful difference to our players and our campaign. We look forward to working closely with him and wish him every success as he begins this exciting new chapter with Delhi Capitals," Grandhi said.Yuvraj Singh excited to begin new chapter with Delhi CapitalsYuvraj expressed his excitement at taking up the new role, describing his existing association with the franchise and its owners as a special part of the opportunity. He also looked forward to working alongside former India captain Sourav Ganguly, popularly known as Dada."I am excited to begin a new chapter in my life with the Delhi Capitals. I have an old association with the franchise and know the owners well, which makes this a special opportunity for me. I’m also looking forward to teaming up with Dada, this time as coaches."Coaching is something I am truly passionate about, and I cannot wait to get started with this extremely talented squad. I’m sure it’s going to be an exciting journey for me, and I look forward to contributing to the team’s success," Yuvraj said.Yuvraj's distinguished IPL careerYuvraj enjoyed a distinguished IPL career, featuring in 132 matches, scoring 2,750 runs and claiming 36 wickets. Renowned for his explosive batting and ability to change games, he was instrumental in India's historic World Cup triumphs in 2007 and 2011.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Josh Hazlewood's career-best six-for helps him leapfrog Brett Lee in Australia's Test wicket-taking history
articles.summary: Josh Hazlewood added another milestone to his illustrious career on Tuesday, surpassing Australian pace legend Brett Lee in the country's list of leading
articles.body: Josh Hazlewood added another milestone to his illustrious career on Tuesday, surpassing Australian pace legend Brett Lee in the country's list of leading Test wicket-takers. The right-arm quick achieved the feat with a career-best six-wicket haul against South Africa in the first Test at Kingsmead in Durban, helping Australia seal a commanding 214-run victory.Hazlewood moves past Brett Lee in Australia's record booksHazlewood returned figures of 6/49 in South Africa's second innings, taking his tally to 311 wickets in Test cricket. He claimed eight wickets across the match, having also picked up two in the first innings, moving past Lee's career tally of 310.The achievement places Hazlewood sixth among Australia's highest wicket-taking fast bowlers and eighth on the country's overall Test wicket-takers list.Shane Warne remains Australia's leading Test wicket-taker with 708 scalps, while Nathan Lyon occupies second place with 573 wickets. Hazlewood is now among the country's most successful fast bowlers, with Mitchell Johnson next on the list at 313 wickets.During the match, Hazlewood also moved past several renowned bowlers in the all-time Test wicket-taking charts, including Kemar Roach, Fred Trueman, Lance Gibbs and Morne Morkel. He drew level with India's Ishant Sharma and Zaheer Khan, who each claimed 311 Test wickets.Hazlewood dismantles South Africa on Day 5Hazlewood's milestone came through a match-winning performance that crushed South Africa's hopes of pulling off an improbable chase. Resuming the final day at 102/4, the hosts needed another 319 runs to reach their target but were eventually bowled out for 206.The Australian pacer broke South Africa's resistance by dismissing Wiaan Mulder, who had battled for 29 runs off 109 deliveries. Hazlewood then removed Marco Jansen for 35 with a delivery that breached his defence before dismissing Simon Harmer in the same over.Mitchell Starc subsequently ended Aiden Markram's determined innings of 75, while Hazlewood returned to claim the final wicket by dismissing Anrich Nortje. His six-wicket haul not only secured Australia's 214-run victory but also delivered a career-best performance in the longest format.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sediqullah Atal creates history, becomes first Afghanistan batter to score fourth-innings Test century
articles.summary: Sediqullah Atal produced a historic fourth-innings century to help Afghanistan secure a draw against Bangladesh in the one-off Test in Abu Dhabi on
articles.body: Sediqullah Atal produced a historic fourth-innings century to help Afghanistan secure a draw against Bangladesh in the one-off Test in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday. The left-handed batter became the first Afghanistan cricketer to score a Test hundred in the fourth innings, smashing 111 off 332 deliveries to deny Bangladesh victory despite a daunting target of 479 runs.Atal's marathon knock featured nine boundaries and three sixes. He brought up his maiden Test century in style, pulling Hasan Mahmud for a boundary before removing his helmet and bowing down in celebration as his teammates applauded the landmark achievement.Atal's marathon innings keeps Afghanistan aliveAfghanistan resumed the final day at 132/3, still needing 347 runs to win. Atal continued to anchor the innings after sharing a crucial partnership with captain Rahmat Shah, who scored 51 off 124 balls.The opener found further support from Hashmatullah Shahidi, who made 36, and wicketkeeper-batter Ikram Alikhil, who contributed 33. Their efforts helped Afghanistan resist Bangladesh's bowling attack and stretch the contest deep into the final day.Atal eventually departed for 111 after facing 332 balls. Taijul Islam ended the historic innings by inducing an edge that was caught by Tanzid Hasan at short leg. Atal reviewed the decision, but the UltraEdge confirmed a faint contact, bringing his marathon effort to an end at 281/7.Qais Ahmad helps Afghanistan secure memorable drawDespite Atal's departure, Afghanistan's lower order refused to give in. Qais Ahmad played a crucial unbeaten knock of 49 off 80 deliveries, while Yamin Ahmadzai remained not out on 19 as the visitors batted through 142 overs in their second innings.Afghanistan eventually finished at 346/8, holding on for a draw after being set a target of 479. The result denied Bangladesh victory despite their strong position heading into the final day.Bangladesh had scored 346 in their first innings before bowling Afghanistan out for 240, gaining a 106-run lead. They then declared their second innings at 372/7, powered by Litton Das's 102 and contributions from Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mushfiqur Rahim, to set Afghanistan a challenging target.Atal's historic century and the resistance from Afghanistan's lower order ensured the one-off Test ended in a draw, turning what looked like a Bangladesh victory into a memorable fightback for the visitors. Litton Das was named Player of the Match for his century and contributions across the game.Brief scores: Bangladesh 346 and 372/7 declared; Afghanistan 240 and 346/8. articles.title: Karun Nair's unbeaten 81 keeps Karnataka afloat after top-order collapse against Andhra
articles.summary: VIJAYAWADA: Dropped without explanation from South Zone’s Duleep Trophy XI six weeks ago, Karun Nair has answered in the language he has learnt well
articles.body: VIJAYAWADA: Dropped without explanation from South Zone’s Duleep Trophy XI six weeks ago, Karun Nair has answered in the language he has learnt well lately, runs under pressure. After an unbeaten century in the Dr (Capt) K Thimmappaiah Memorial Tournament recently, the 34-year-old dug Karnataka out of trouble with an unbeaten 81 (130b; 8x4; 2x6) against Andhra in their Ranji Trophy season opener on Tuesday, keeping alive their hopes of salvaging a draw.With Karnataka trailing by 144 runs on the first innings at the ACA Stadium here, the experienced opening pair of Mayank Agarwal (18) and KL Rahul (1) fell cheaply to leave the visitors reeling at 25/2. Karun, however, held his nerve, counterattacked when the opportunity arose and stitched together a 94-run stand with Manvanth Kumar (44) before combining with R Smaran to steer Karnataka to 176/4 in 60 overs, a lead of 32 runs heading into the final day.Having conceded the first-innings lead, Karnataka fought to keep the prospect of a draw and a point alive, reaching 176/4 in 60 overs with a slender 32-run lead heading into the final day.Earlier, Andhra were bowled out for 418 in 121.5 overs, with spinner Shikhar Shetty claiming a six-wicket haul after a long toil.Resuming at 331/4, Andhra lost centurion Seeram Rahul (119) when he was cramped for room by Ritesh Bhatkal (2/109). The teenage debutant added 11 to his overnight score of 108 before departing. Useful contributions from Venkat Sasikanth (39) and Saurabh Kumar (24) took the hosts past 400.Facing a deficit of 144, Mayank and Rahul began cautiously, but Andhra’s astute field placements left the experienced duo with little room even to rotate the strike.Left-arm spinner Saurabh Kumar (3/41) proved particularly effective, using flight and guile to trouble the openers. He nearly had Rahul in the final over before lunch, but an appeal for a catch behind was turned down. The reprieve did little to help the Karnataka batter, who was trapped in front by Saurabh for a laborious one off 20 deliveries. In his next over, the 33-year-old, who moved to Andhra from Uttar Pradesh last season, trapped Mayank to leave Karnataka precariously placed.KV Aneesh (6) was the next to fall, edging Saurabh to skipper Ricky Bhui at first slip. Promoted to No. 3, Manvanth Kumar (44) joined Karun, and the pair set about rebuilding after Manvanth was dropped on seven.Karun eased the pressure with two sixes off Saurabh and Lalith Mohan in successive overs. As Andhra’s bowlers began to stray in line and length, the Karnataka duo grew in confidence. Karun remained a picture of composure, bringing up his half-century off 76 deliveries.Their 94-run fourth-wicket stand ended when Manvanth played back to a Lalith delivery and dragged it onto his stumps.First-innings centurion Smaran then joined Karun, and the pair wore down the Andhra attack with sharp running between the wickets. With Karun holding firm and Smaran providing support, Karnataka moved into a position from which they could realistically save the match.ScoreboardKarnataka (I innings): 274Andhra (I innings; O/N 331/6): SV Rahul lbw Bhatkal 119, Venkat Sasikanth lbw Shikhar 39, Saurabh Kumar c Shrijith b Shikhar 24, Lalith Mohan (not out) 16, Kavuri Saiteja lbw Shikhar 1. Extras: (B-5; LB-5, WD-1; NB-4) 15. articles.title: WTC 2025-27 points table: South Africa crash out of top two after Durban defeat; where does India stand?
articles.summary: South Africa have slipped to third place in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) 2025-27 standings following their 214-run defeat to Australia in the
articles.body: South Africa have slipped to third place in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) 2025-27 standings following their 214-run defeat to Australia in the first Test at Durban. The result has strengthened Australia's position at the top of the table, while New Zealand have moved into second place.The defending champions entered the series in second place but dropped to third after suffering their second defeat in five matches in the current WTC cycle. South Africa now have a points percentage (PCT) of 60.00, while New Zealand sit second with 72.22 per cent.Australia, meanwhile, consolidated their position at the summit with nine wins from 11 matches, taking their points percentage to 81.82. Bangladesh and India occupy fourth and fifth places, respectively, with points percentages of 55.56 and 51.52.Updated WTC 2025-27 standingsPos.TeamPlayedWonLostDrawDed.PointsPCT (%)1Australia11920010881.822New Zealand641105272.223South Africa532003660.004Bangladesh632104055.565India1154206851.526England16781147438.547Sri Lanka612302433.338West Indies1228223020.839Pakistan92701954.63PCT: Percentage of points earned. Ded.: Points deducted.Hazlewood, Renshaw power Australia to dominant Durban victoryAustralia secured the 214-run win at Kingsmead after Josh Hazlewood produced a career-best performance of 6/49 on the fifth day. South Africa, chasing a target of 421, were bowled out for 206 despite Aiden Markram's fighting 75 off 237 deliveries and Marco Jansen's 35.Hazlewood broke the hosts' resistance by dismissing Wiaan Mulder for 29 before removing Jansen and Simon Harmer in the same over. Mitchell Starc then ended Markram's determined innings, while Hazlewood claimed the final wicket by dismissing Anrich Nortje.The foundation for Australia's victory was laid by Matt Renshaw, who scored a magnificent 190 in the first innings and followed it up with 82 in the second. Australia posted 390 before declaring their second innings at 314/6, setting South Africa a challenging target.South Africa had managed 284 in their first innings but struggled to sustain their chase on the final day. The defeat also marked Temba Bavuma's first loss as South Africa's Test captain.Renshaw was named Player of the Match for his outstanding contributions with the bat and ball. Australia now lead the three-match Test series 1-0.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
